direction.premise: A public court of three factions conceals two simultaneous political orders.
direction.composition: The court illustration and three seven-position faction tracks sit above a five-order control table.
direction.shapeLanguage: Pixel court portraits, seven square influence cells and small crown counters form a compact political instrument.
direction.surfaceAndMaterial: Warm bronze panels surround the original pixel court illustration and flat faction tracks.
direction.paletteLogic: Army red, treasury ochre and people green distinguish the three persistent influence tracks against violet court panels.
direction.typography: The original serif court headings and compact sans-serif action effects retain their hierarchy.
direction.signature: Two hidden political orders reveal together and push the three public faction tracks in different directions.
direction.distinction: FOG uses geographic orders and ZAMAZKA uses painted restoration fragments; this port retains its source game object and the specific input loop described here.

architecture.primaryVerb: Choose a public stance, seal one of five political orders, then inspect its simultaneous resolution against the opponent.
architecture.physicalFeedback: Sealing an order locks that choice; both orders appear together and leave changed tracks, marks and history.
architecture.spatialRationale: The court illustration and three seven-position faction tracks sit above a five-order control table. This keeps the current game object and its real inputs spatially connected on a phone.

production.renderer: DOM faction cells and the source pixel court illustration preserve discrete influence values and legible action effects.
production.focalAsset: The retained court illustration animates the relationship between the army, treasury and people; the authored throne icon shows their three colored pillars.

motion.character: Sealing an order locks that choice; both orders appear together and leave changed tracks, marks and history.
motion.action: Choose a public stance, seal one of five political orders, then inspect its simultaneous resolution against the opponent.
motion.anticipation: The current selection, room state and available control labels expose the pending operation before the player activates it.
motion.response: The next visible state responds to the actual control: Two hidden political orders reveal together and push the three public faction tracks in different directions.
motion.followThrough: The resulting world, board or round state remains visible until a later explicit action changes it; no decorative transition hides the outcome.
motion.interruption: Repeated input uses the current state; pointer cancellation releases held controls and hidden tabs stop transmitting held actions.
motion.reducedMotion: The complete play state remains legible without decorative entry animations; spatial gameplay and authoritative outcomes retain their original timing.

evidence.expectedChange: A new political court opens with three neutral influence tracks and a required first public stance.
